text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- A consortium in which Schiphol USA holds a 40 pct stake takes over new terminal at New York's JFK international airport. (p1)
- Health service pension fund PGGM aims to raise the premiums of its participants. (p1)
- Spanish province of Catalonia holds the Netherlands responsible for recent outbreak of swine fever in their region. (p1)
- Rotterdam considers extension of its port of greater importance than standard of life according to reports of its advice to transport ministry. (p1)
- Britain's pharma concern Zeneca takes over Leiden-based biotech firm MoGen. (p3)
- Publisher PCM books 25 pct lower 1996 net although turnover doubles due to takeover of Dagbladunie. (p3)
- Dutch inflation in April reaches lowest level this year at 1.8 pct. (p5)
- Many sectors of industry have problems finding qualified staff. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- Extension of the port of Rotterdam and Schiphol airport will hardly contribute to economic growth, according to professor of Delft University. (p1)
- KPN Dutch PTT chief Wim Dik named as parliamentary party D66's head of list of candidates. (p1)
- Automation company Baan takes over U.S. rival Aurum Software. (p2)
- Senior staff of Akzo Nobel reject proposed on 36-hours working week. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- One year sentence demanded for the man who threatenend repeatedly to kill Queen Beatrix. (p1)
- Steel concern Hoogovens wants 25 million guilders from the state for cleaning strongly polluted part of factory site. (p2)
- Engineering firms Fugro and Grabowsky & Poort
develop plan for airport in the North Sea. (p23)
- Price war threatens in saturated Dutch beer market. (p23)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Retailer combine De Boer Unigro has ambitious plans for the future with ten percent yearly profits growth target. (p13)
- Insurer Stad Rotterdam's Q1 net up at Dfl 31.6 million from Dfl 27.7 million. (p13)
TROUW
- Tugging concern Smit Internationale takes new steps against hostile takeovers. (p7)
- Dutch Rail NS withdraws decision to sell parts of its construction unit to external builders. (p7)
